title: Verifier‑Grounded Generate–Verify–Repair for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks: a Paired Mininet Emulation Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study that measured whether a verifier‑grounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) loop reduces operationally detectable policy‑violation errors when a hosted LLM generates network configuration sequences from operator intent in a Mininet emulation. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics (the same sampled initial candidate was reused for baseline and guarded pairs), N=200 paired intents were executed across three vendor‑template families and four topology patterns. The guarded pipeline permitted deterministic validation and a single verifier‑triggered repair. Baseline success rate (no policy violation detected) was 196/200 (98%); guarded success was 200/200 (100%). The paired risk difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.02 (95% bootstrap CI 0.005–0.04); exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.125. Four validator‑triggered repairs were invoked (4 additional model calls total), each corresponding to a discordant pair; mean extra model calls per intent = 0.02 and per avoided violation = 1.0. The confirmatory result did not reach conventional statistical significance; exploratory diagnostics show GVR corrected all observed mechanically detectable violations in this emulation at marginal model‑call cost. We report full preregistration, execution, deterministic verifier traces, and analysis artifacts and discuss threats to validity and operational implications within the study scope.

sections.introduction: LLM assistance for network operations (NetOps) promises faster intent→configuration translation but raises safety and correctness concerns: generated artifacts may contain syntax, topology, or policy violations with operational impact. Prior prototype work demonstrates that pairing generation with deterministic verifiers or verifier‑grounded repair loops can reduce mechanically verifiable errors in narrow scenarios [1], [2], [3]. Open questions remain about scaling such patterns across heterogeneous vendor templates and realistic topology patterns. We conducted a preregistered paired experiment to estimate the effect of a verifier‑grounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline versus single‑shot LLM generation on operationally detectable policy violations in a controlled Mininet emulation. Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired design under shared_initial_candidate semantics; (2) a reproducible Mininet‑based emulation using provenance‑traced synthetic intent→configuration tasks across vendor/template strata; (3) confirmatory paired analysis with exact McNemar testing and bootstrap CIs; and (4) an evidence‑grounded failure analysis and limitations discussion.
sections.related_work: Recent NetOps and AIOps surveys document rapid growth of LLM‑for‑NetOps research while noting gaps in operationally meaningful benchmarks and verifier integration [4], [5]. Prototype studies show GPT‑class models can produce draft router configurations but often introduce syntax, topology, and semantic errors; verified prompt programming and verifier‑grounded repair have been proposed to mitigate these faults [1], [2]. Cross‑domain work on Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) and verifier‑grounded frameworks demonstrates utility when deterministic or formal oracles exist (code compilation, formal semantics, contract checking) but also highlights dependence on oracle coverage [2], [3]. Our study builds on this empirical pattern and tests a constrained, provenance‑traced GVR instantiation in network configuration emulation.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and experimental design: We preregistered study C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1 prior to execution. The research question: Does a verifier‑grounded GVR loop reduce per‑intent operationally detectable policy violations versus LLM‑only generation in Mininet emulation? Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Design: paired binary outcomes on N=200 unique intents (baseline and guarded per intent), stratified across 3 vendor‑template families and 4 topology patterns. Sampling, exclusions, analysis, and sensitivity rules were frozen and are archived with the execution artifacts. Model and generation semantics: all generations used the hosted model identifier gpt‑5‑mini (declared_model_version). The archived model configuration shows temperature=null/unset; preregistered methods explicitly note that temperature=null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature=0. Generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate: exactly one sampled initial generation per pair was reused by baseline and guarded. The guarded condition applied deterministic validator checks and permitted up to one verifier‑triggered repair call; the baseline outcome was the single initial candidate without repair. Execution environment and validators: tasks were executed in a Mininet‑style emulation harness (see artifact bundle). A deterministic netops validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) checked syntactic correctness, reachability/topology constraints, and policy/ACL constraints; validator traces were archived per episode. Budget and call limits: task_count=200, planned_episode_count=400, maximum_model_calls=400, initial_generation_calls_per_task=1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task=1. Shared_initial_candidate semantics and the paired design mean outcome differences can only arise from permitted downstream deterministic validation and any permitted repair actions.
sections.results: Execution and primary outcome: Execution completed per the preregistration (completed_episode_count=400; model_calls_used=204; provider audit: shared_initial_generation=200, repair=4). Confirmatory paired analysis (N=200 pairs) produced baseline success (no policy violation) 196/200 and guarded success 200/200. Contingency counts: n11=196, n10=4 (guarded success when baseline failed), n01=0, n00=0. Paired risk difference = 0.02 (guarded−baseline). Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 0.125. Bootstrap (paired) 95% CI for risk difference (percentile) = [0.005, 0.04] (bootstrap_seed=1729, 10,000 resamples). Repairs and cost: four verifier‑triggered repair calls were invoked across the study (repair stage count = 4). Total model calls = 204 → mean model calls per intent = 1.02; mean extra calls per intent due to guarded repairs = 0.02. Each avoided policy violation corresponded to one repair call here (mean extra calls per avoided violation = 1.0). Exploratory diagnostics: every observed baseline policy violation (4 cases) was corrected in the guarded pipeline after the single permitted repair; no other discordant directions (guarded failing where baseline succeeded) were observed.
sections.discussion: Interpretation: Within the preregistered Mininet emulation scope and under shared_initial_candidate semantics, a verifier‑grounded GVR loop corrected all observed mechanically detectable policy violations at very low additional model‑call cost. The observed paired risk difference (2 percentage points) favored guarded but did not reach conventional statistical significance (p=0.125) for N=200. The bootstrap CI excludes large negative effects and suggests the absolute improvement is small but potentially operationally meaningful when violations are high‑cost. Operational implications: when deterministic validators that provide localized feedback are available, a modest verifier‑triggered repair budget can address certain classes of mechanically detectable errors (syntax, reachability, ACL violations) with low call overhead; however, the practical benefit depends on baseline failure prevalence and verifier coverage.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired study that compared single‑shot LLM generation to a verifier‑grounded GVR pipeline for intent→configuration tasks in a controlled Mininet emulation. Guarded GVR eliminated the four observed baseline policy violations at the cost of four repair calls (mean extra calls per intent 0.02), producing a 2 percentage‑point paired improvement (95% CI 0.005–0.04) that did not reach statistical significance (p=0.125). These artifact‑grounded results demonstrate that verifier‑guided repair can correct mechanically verifiable faults in this emulation at low model‑call cost, but they do not establish general production readiness. Future work should expand verifier coverage, include multiple models and real vendor devices, and evaluate semantic policy detection gaps that deterministic verifiers may miss.

disclosure_statement: This Autonomous Agent research run used hosted LLMs and deterministic validators per the preregistered study C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1. Models/tools: declared model gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses); adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1; deterministic netops validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5; Mininet‑style emulation harness and synthetic task generator deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt pre‑lock; after the autonomy lock the AI autonomously performed literature verification, study selection, preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, revision, and manuscript drafting. Preregistration: the study was preregistered (C1‑GVR‑multivendor‑2026‑v1) and frozen prior to execution; the preregistration hash is recorded in the archived bundle. Master prompt: archived initial master prompt reference path provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Generation semantics and temperature: the execution used shared_initial_candidate generation semantics (the same sampled initial candidate was reused for baseline and guarded pairs). The model configuration records temperature=null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature=0. Exactly one sampled initial generation per pair was produced and shared; only downstream deterministic validation and the predeclared permitted repair calls could create paired outcome differences. Preregistered limits and execution: task_count=200 paired intents, maximum_model_calls=400; actual model_calls_used=204; repair calls invoked=4. No human manual editing of manuscript technical content occurred after the autonomy lock. Complete execution artifacts, verifier traces, raw model outputs, analysis code, and manifests are archived with the evidence bundle.
limitations: Scope limited to Mininet‑style emulation with synthetic, provenance‑traced intent→configuration tasks; results do not directly generalize to production hardware or live operational environments.
Single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini) was evaluated; multi‑model generality is not established.

Deterministic validator coverage was limited to mechanically checkable errors (syntax, reachability, ACL/policy encodings); high‑level semantic or specification misinterpretations outside the validator’s oracle may remain undetected.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics mean observed paired differences could only arise from validator‑triggered repair; this design does not measure effects of alternative generation prompting strategies or multi‑sample candidate selection.

The confirmatory effect size (2 percentage points) did not reach statistical significance at α=0.05 for N=200; larger samples or higher baseline failure prevalence would be needed to demonstrate small absolute improvements with high confidence.
